title: IELTS Academic 21 - Listening Test 3 - Part 3
transcriptHtml:
LISTENING TRANSCRIPT - PART 3

💡 Audio-Track Sync: Bấm vào bất kỳ câu nào dưới đây để phát audio ngay đúng câu đó!

13:56ANNOUNCER: You will hear part of a discussion between two textile students about their research into sustainable fashion.
14:05ANNOUNCER: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 24.
14:31ANNOUNCER: Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 24.
14:40MADDY: Shall we go through our research for our sustainable fashion project?
14:44RYAN: Good idea. I think I've done enough reading now.
14:47MADDY: Me too. I've learnt such a lot about what sustainability actually means.
14:52RYAN: Mmm, same for me with ethical fashion. I didn't really appreciate the difference between that and sustainable fashion before doing this research.
15:02MADDY: I know – most people use these terms interchangeably – but in fact the difference is quite distinct when you think about it. Sustainable relates to the environment and ethical relates more to the way workers or animals are treated.
15:14RYAN: I totally understand why people get confused, though. There are so many other terms used – like 'eco-friendly', which is actually quite meaningless.
15:22MADDY: And the way companies use these terms when describing their products doesn't help. They're often deliberately vague, I think, and don't provide enough information about how their products are made.
15:33RYAN: Yes.
15:35MADDY: It was interesting to read about the debates surrounding wool production and how ethical and sustainable that is. It's generally considered to be sustainable because it's a natural product.
15:46RYAN: And it also lasts a long time and can be recycled. All very positive. But I wasn't convinced by the argument that wool production is sustainable because it doesn't use many chemicals – what about all the fungicides and insecticides used in sheep farming?
16:02MADDY: Good point. And I couldn't find any evidence for the claim about sheep farming being better for the environment than cattle farming.
16:13RYAN: No – they're both really bad. I read different reports about how unethical it is to even shear sheep. Some people say it's cruel but as long as the sheep are kept in good condition I can't see anything wrong with it.
16:25MADDY: Me neither.
16:30ANNOUNCER: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 25 to 30.
17:10ANNOUNCER: Now listen and answer questions 25 to 30.
17:18RYAN: Shall we talk about some of the semi-synthetic new fabrics now?
17:22MADDY: OK, let's do that.
17:24RYAN: Let's start with Lyocell, I've been reading about that.
17:28MADDY: Yeah, that's the one produced from the pulp of eucalyptus trees, isn't it?
17:32RYAN: Yes, and what happens with that is really impressive. Over 99% of dissolving agents used in the manufacturing process are used again.
17:43MADDY: Yeah. Now, there are a few semi-synthetic fabrics that I'd never heard of. Like Cupro, for example.
17:50RYAN: Made from byproducts of the cotton industry to create a kind of vegan silk. But I'm not sure how sustainable this really is as there are so many reports of pollution caused by the manufacturing process.
18:03MADDY: Mmm. It doesn't compare favourably with all the other sustainable fabrics we've looked at, no.
18:10RYAN: Bamboo is one fabric we're all familiar with. But I didn't know that it was only organic bamboo that's truly sustainable.
18:19MADDY: Me neither. Apparently, the manufacturing process for a significant proportion of bamboo is chemically quite intensive – which obviously can be quite damaging.
18:32RYAN: EcoVero is an example of a semi-synthetic fabric which is becoming really popular.
18:38MADDY: Probably because manufacturing causes 50 percent fewer emissions and takes up half as much energy as conventional fabrics. That saves production costs as well as being better for the environment.
18:53RYAN: That's true. I think demand for cork will continue to grow. It works really well in vegan shoes and bags.
19:02MADDY: Mmm and it's the only fabric that's fundamentally sustainable – the cork trees it comes from are renewable and the product itself is both recyclable and biodegradable – which is unique.
19:17RYAN: And the harvesting process is actually good for the trees. There are no downsides to using this source at all.
19:25MADDY: Hemp is another really good sustainable fabric from a natural source.
19:30RYAN: Yes. Did you know that clothes made from hemp protect the wearer from the sun and it's also antibacterial?
19:39MADDY: No, I didn't. But I did read that it's quite hard to grow, so perhaps that's why it's not as common as you'd think.
19:47RYAN: I'm sure that'll change.
19:55ANNOUNCER: That is the end of Part 3.
19:58ANNOUNCER: You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to Part 3.

groups.title: Questions 21 and 22
groups.instructions:
Choose TWO letters, A–E.
Which TWO points do the speakers make about the terms 'ethical' and 'sustainable' fashion?

groups.title: Questions 23 and 24
groups.instructions:
Choose TWO letters, A–E.
Which TWO claims about wool production do the speakers disagree with?

groups.title: Questions 25–30
groups.instructions:
What comment do the speakers make about each of the following semi-synthetic fabrics?
Choose SIX answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–H, next to Questions 25–30.

options.text: The production process is fuel efficient.
It is the least sustainable of alternative fabrics.
It is not durable in the long-term.
It needs to be produced in a certain way to be sustainable.
Chemicals required for production can be reused.
This is from a wholly sustainable source.

options: A. Their definitions keep changing.
B. People think they mean the same thing.
C. The term 'eco-friendly' is preferable.
D. They are often used imprecisely.
E. Companies should avoid using them on clothing labels.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B (People think they mean the same thing)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'most people use these terms interchangeably'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'use interchangeably' = think they mean the same thing.

options: A. Their definitions keep changing.
B. People think they mean the same thing.
C. The term 'eco-friendly' is preferable.
D. They are often used imprecisely.
E. Companies should avoid using them on clothing labels.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: D (They are often used imprecisely)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'They're often deliberately vague, I think, and don't provide enough information...'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'deliberately vague' = used imprecisely.

q23.text: Claims about wool production they disagree with (First choice):
options: A. Sheep are generally well-treated.
B. Wool is easy to recycle.
C. Wool is a long-lasting fabric.
D. Wool production involves few chemicals.
E. Sheep do less environmental damage than other livestock.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: D (Wool production involves few chemicals)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'I wasn't convinced by the argument that wool production is sustainable because it doesn't use many chemicals – what about all the fungicides and insecticides...'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'wasn't convinced that it doesn't use many chemicals' = disagree with claim that it involves few chemicals.

q24.text: Claims about wool production they disagree with (Second choice):
options: A. Sheep are generally well-treated.
B. Wool is easy to recycle.
C. Wool is a long-lasting fabric.
D. Wool production involves few chemicals.
E. Sheep do less environmental damage than other livestock.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: E (Sheep do less environmental damage than other livestock)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'I couldn't find any evidence for the claim about sheep farming being better for the environment than cattle farming. RYAN: No – they're both really bad.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'couldn't find evidence for sheep farming being better than cattle' = disagree that sheep do less damage.
• Đáp án đúng: G (Chemicals required for production can be reused)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'Over 99% of dissolving agents used in the manufacturing process are used again.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'dissolving agents' = chemicals; 'used again' = can be reused.
• Đáp án đúng: B (It is the least sustainable of alternative fabrics)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'It doesn't compare favourably with all the other sustainable fabrics we've looked at, no.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'doesn't compare favourably with all other sustainable fabrics' = least sustainable.
• Đáp án đúng: F (It needs to be produced in a certain way to be sustainable)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'it was only organic bamboo that's truly sustainable... manufacturing process for a significant proportion of bamboo is chemically quite intensive...'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'only organic bamboo that's truly sustainable' = needs to be produced in a certain way (organically) to be sustainable.
• Đáp án đúng: A (The production process is fuel efficient)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'manufacturing causes 50 percent fewer emissions and takes up half as much energy as conventional fabrics.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'takes up half as much energy' = fuel efficient.
• Đáp án đúng: H (This is from a wholly sustainable source)

• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'it's the only fabric that's fundamentally sustainable – the cork trees it comes from are renewable and the product itself is both recyclable and biodegradable... harvesting process is actually good for the trees. There are no downsides to using this source at all.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'fundamentally sustainable / no downsides at all' = wholly sustainable source.
• Đáp án đúng: D (It provides additional health benefits)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'clothes made from hemp protect the wearer from the sun and it's also antibacterial'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'protect from the sun and antibacterial' = additional health benefits.
